desc: Analyze the problem: Sum of $B^p$ over all completions of zero-entries in matrix $A$, modulo $p$.
Derive mathematical properties: For $p>2$, only terms with exactly one zero-entry raised to power $p-1$ and one non-zero entry raised to power 1 survive summation. For $p=2$, all paths survive.
Formulate algorithm for $p>2$: Iterate over zero-edges $(u,v)$. If $A_{v,u} \neq 0$, add contributions to result matrix based on parity of $p$ and position of the non-zero edge in the path.
Formulate algorithm for $p=2$: Construct $B$ with zeros replaced by 1, compute $B^2 \pmod 2$.
Implement solution in Python handling both cases.
